title: Choose your home island
text: Welcome to the Old Coast, governor. Your sloop carries the company's planks and sails, and its gold is yours to spend. Every island is open to you: look at their fertilities and deposits, sail to the one you want as your home and found a Trading Post there. Its pier stands on the water; it stores the island's goods and receives your ships.

title: Roads from the Trading Post
text: Nothing reaches the Trading Post without a road: lay ten tiles of dirt road leading away from it. Roads cost nothing, and every building they connect delivers to the Trading Post or a Warehouse.

title: Timber for the colony
text: Every house and workshop needs planks. Build a lumberjack in the forest and a sawmill, and connect both to the Trading Post by road. The company sends planks to get you started. Goods beyond the Trading Post capacity of the island you choose are lost.

title: Room for settlers
text: Settlers pay taxes, and they are the workers of your workshops. Build four settler houses along the road.

title: Fish for the table
text: Hungry settlers neither grow nor pay their full taxes. Build a fisher with its jetty on the water and connect it to the Trading Post. Here are more planks for houses. Goods beyond the Trading Post capacity of the island you choose are lost.

title: A market square
text: Settlers want a market within reach of their houses. Build a small market and connect it to the road.

title: Warm clothes
text: Well-dressed settlers are content, and content settlers become citizens one day. Build a sheep farm and a wool weaver and connect both to the Trading Post.

title: A place of worship
text: Citizens will only settle in a town with a chapel. Build one and connect it to the road.

title: A growing town
text: Fed and housed settlers move in on their own. Grow the archipelago to 120 settlers: with a market and a chapel, citizens may then arrive. These planks are for more houses. Goods beyond the Trading Post capacity of the island you choose are lost.

title: A second settlement
text: Beyond the bay lies a second island with iron in its hills. Load your sloop with planks for a Trading Post and sail there to found a settlement. Here are planks for its first buildings. Goods beyond the Trading Post capacity of the island you choose are lost.

title: Tools from the second island
text: Citizens' workshops need tools. Mine iron, smelt it and make tools where the iron is, and let a sloop on a route bring them home: store ten tools in a Trading Post.

title: The first citizens
text: Upgrade a full settler house whose needs are all met into a citizen house. Its walls need stone: quarry it on an island with stone deposits.

title: A shipyard of our own
text: Citizens open the way to shipbuilding. Build a shipyard with its slipway in the water: the company sends the sails for your first new sloop. Goods beyond the Trading Post capacity of the island you choose are lost.

title: A second sloop
text: One sloop cannot sail a route and found islands at once. Order a sloop at the shipyard.

title: A tavern for the town
text: Citizens want a tavern, a market and a chapel within reach. Build a tavern and connect it to the road.

title: Letters and numbers
text: A school serves the citizens around it like the tavern does: each service in reach adds to their contentment. Build a school and connect it to the road.

title: Cheese for the table
text: Citizens eat bread or cheese, and both together feed them best. Build a dairy farm with its pastures and a cheese dairy, and connect both to the Trading Post.

title: A church for the merchants
text: Merchants want a church besides the market, chapel, tavern and school. Build a church and connect it to the road. Merchant houses need bricks as well: dig clay on an island with clay deposits and fire it in a brickworks.

title: The first merchants
text: Upgrade a full citizen house whose needs are all met into a merchant house. Its walls need bricks.

title: Sausages and pies
text: Merchants eat sausages or pies, and both together feed them best. Have a butcher and a pastry kitchen at work, both connected to the Trading Post.

title: Beer and brandy
text: Merchants drink beer or brandy, and both together please them best. Have a brewery and a distillery at work, both connected to the Trading Post.

title: A brig for the routes
text: A brig carries four loads where a sloop carries two. Order a brig at the shipyard.

title: Bricks for the theatre
text: A theatre needs thirty bricks. Store thirty bricks in a Trading Post.

title: A cathedral for the patricians
text: Patricians want a university and a cathedral besides the services the merchants enjoy. Build a cathedral and connect it to the road. Its windows need glass: quarry quartz on an island with quartz deposits and melt it in a glass smelter.

title: The first patricians
text: Upgrade a full merchant house whose needs are all met into a patrician house. Its windows need glass.

title: Roast beef and oysters
text: Patricians eat roast beef or oysters, and both together feed them best. Have a slaughterhouse and an oyster house at work, both connected to the Trading Post.

title: Wine and grain spirit
text: Patricians drink wine or grain spirit, and both together please them best. Have a winepress and a grain distillery at work, both connected to the Trading Post.

title: Glass for the houses
text: Every patrician house needs three glass, and the optician grinds spectacles from it. Store thirty glass in a Trading Post.

title: A galleon for the routes
text: A galleon carries six loads of sixty where a brig carries four of fifty. Order a galleon at the shipyard.
